questions: How many nano-SQUIDs did you measure in all, and how many showed a zero-bias peak that appears at the half-flux transition? You name devices A, B and C and "a series of devices with two functioning tunnel contacts" (p. 4).
Why were the other devices set aside: tunnel junctions that failed (yield "below 50%", p. 5), or other reasons?
Which ranges of gate voltage, field angle and temperature did you measure beyond those shown, and at which VG were Fig. 3b-e taken?
What does the second-best device or dataset look like? Device C answers this in part (Supp. Note S1.E); is there a second single-probe device like A, or a second cooldown of A?

How was the third derivative behind Fig. 4c, f, i and l computed (smoothing, bias window, the threshold between "correlated" and "no correlation"), and does the fraction in Fig. 4l change with those choices?
What series and line resistances were subtracted from the local tunnel spectra, and could you show raw curves for Fig. 1f and Fig. 3b-c?
At higher bias, do the zero-field gate maps (Fig. 4a-b) show Coulomb-like resonances or levels that split and recross, which would point to a dot at the tunnel contact?

A trivial asymmetric SQUID also gives a diode efficiency of zero and a sign change at half flux. What in Fig. 1e, Fig. 3a or Supp. Fig. S4 separates the topological phase jump from that case, for example the abruptness of the sign change, or your model run at a trivial chemical potential?
